name: Build Your Own Strategy
tagline: Compose reusable multi-step functions to conquer winding corridors.
narrative:
The Snake Corridor is an 11x11 winding path that requires the robot to repeatedly turn into open side passages and step forward.

Writing separate turn and step rules over and over makes your intelligence cluttered. Instead, use the Functions tab to build a custom reusable action: a sequence that turns left and takes a step in one package.

Rules decide when to execute the function, while the function handles the fixed sequence of actions.
objective: Solve the 11×11 Snake Corridor and use at least one custom multi-step function.
learningObjective: Separate decision logic from action sequences: rules choose when to run a function, and functions package multi-step moves.
intelligenceExplanation:
The starting brain unlocks custom Functions. Build a new function (e.g. `turn-left-and-step`) that sequences `pivot-left` followed by `step`.

Your rules then call this custom function whenever the left side is open, keeping your brain clean and modular.
hint: Compose a custom function with pivot-left + step, then trigger it with WHEN !wallLeft.
hints: Functions group actions together; they don't contain WHEN checks.
Create a 2-step function: pivot-left then step.
Order your rules: 1) atGoal -> hold, 2) !wallLeft -> custom-function, 3) !wallAhead -> step, 4) always -> pivot-right.
brief: Create a custom cornering function and use rules to navigate the Snake Corridor.
context: The Snake Corridor winds back and forth. Repeating turn-then-step actions manually makes rules repetitive.
